t: You're at the Royal Academy of Music in Westminster, one of the oldest music schools in the United Kingdom. It was founded in 1822 by John Fane and Nicolas-Charles Bochsa, and received its royal charter in 1830 from King George IV, with the support of the first Duke of Wellington. Fane, the eleventh Earl of Westmorland, was a soldier and politician, but also a diplomat, composer and musician, which helps explain why he cared to start a school like this.
